scope.service: Nyaymalaw is an India-only legal-work system for advocates and firms. This review packet covers account administration, matter intake and work, conflict screening, retrieval, drafting, export, support, security, billing, processors, backups and telemetry. It separates present law from notified future duties and product policy from legal compulsion.
operating_assumptions: The advocate or firm chooses why matter material is collected and how legal work is performed.
NM processes matter content only on documented customer instructions and separately determines purposes for its own account, billing and service-security operations.
India-region storage and no unapproved egress are stricter product policies, not a claim that the DPDP Act universally localises personal data.
Synthetic local work remains permitted; this packet does not authorise confidential pilot or production data.
excluded_without_separate_review: Any jurisdiction outside India or any practice-area promise not named in an approved coverage pack.
Sector-specific regulated workloads, including banking, insurance, securities, health and government data.
Children, biometric identification, voice biometrics, courtroom recording, sealed records and special-category matter protocols.
Cross-border processors, provider training on matter data, automated filing or sending, and direct client communication by NM.

legal_sources.title: Digital Personal Data Protection Act, 2023
legal_sources.authority: Parliament of India / Ministry of Electronics and Information Technology
legal_sources.commencement: Assented on 11 August 2023; individual provisions commence only on dates appointed under section 1(2), now specified by G.S.R. 843(E).
legal_sources.applies_to: Digital personal data within the Act's territorial and material scope when the relevant provisions are in force.
legal_sources.claim_boundary: Definitions and commenced institutional provisions may be used now; future processing duties, permissions, rights, breach duties and exemptions must not be represented as currently operative.

legal_sources.title: DPDP Act commencement notification
legal_sources.authority: Ministry of Electronics and Information Technology
legal_sources.commencement: Sections 1(2), 2, 18-26, 35, 38-43 and 44(1),(3) commenced on publication; section 6(9) and 27(1)(d) commence on 13 November 2026; sections 3-5, 6(1)-(8),(10), 7-17, the remainder of 27, 28-34, 36, 37 and 44(2) commence on 13 May 2027.
legal_sources.applies_to: Determines which DPDP Act provisions are law in force on the review date.
legal_sources.claim_boundary: India-only operation is a product scope and not blanket localisation; section 16 permits notified cross-border restrictions when operative rather than declaring a universal localisation rule.

legal_sources.title: Digital Personal Data Protection Rules, 2025
legal_sources.authority: Ministry of Electronics and Information Technology
legal_sources.commencement: Rules 1, 2 and 17-21 commenced on publication; rule 4 commences on 13 November 2026; rules 3, 5-16, 22 and 23 commence on 13 May 2027. The MeitY register also lists a 16 December 2025 corrigendum, which counsel must check against the operative text.
legal_sources.applies_to: Operational detail under the DPDP Act only when the corresponding rule and enabling Act provision are in force.
legal_sources.claim_boundary: Future rule 6 security safeguards, rule 7 breach notices, rule 8 erasure periods and rule 15 transfer restrictions are design inputs, not present-tense compliance claims.

legal_sources.title: Information Technology Act, 2000
legal_sources.commencement: Current consolidated Act. Section 43A remains in the Act until DPDP Act section 44(2) commences on 13 May 2027; sections 70B and 72A remain separately material.
legal_sources.applies_to: Computer resources, current SPDI security liability, CERT-In powers and disclosure in breach of lawful contract, subject to the provision and facts.
legal_sources.claim_boundary: Section 43A is not a complete privacy code and does not displace contract, privilege, professional duties or sector-specific law.

legal_sources.title: Information Technology (Reasonable Security Practices and Procedures and Sensitive Personal Data or Information) Rules, 2011
legal_sources.authority: Department of Information Technology / India Code
legal_sources.commencement: Published and operative from 11 April 2011; remains relevant with section 43A during the transition to DPDP section 44(2).
legal_sources.applies_to: Body corporates handling defined SPDI, including consent/notice, purpose and necessity, retention, disclosure and reasonable security requirements where applicable.
legal_sources.claim_boundary: SPDI is a defined subset; the rule cannot be used to treat every matter fact identically or to omit professional confidentiality for non-SPDI.

legal_sources.title: MeitY clarification on the SPDI Rules
legal_sources.authority: Ministry of Communications and Information Technology
legal_sources.commencement: Official clarification issued after the SPDI Rules; not a substitute for the Act, Rules or facts.
legal_sources.applies_to: Clarifies the treatment of a service provider processing under contract for another legal entity, including the stated Rules 5 and 6 distinction.
legal_sources.claim_boundary: The clarification does not create a blanket exemption for NM's own purposes, erase Rule 4, or determine the parties' roles without the actual service and contracts.

legal_sources.title: CERT-In directions under section 70B(6) of the IT Act
legal_sources.instrument: CERT-In Directions dated 28 April 2022 and official FAQs
legal_sources.commencement: The directions became effective sixty days after issue and remain a current incident-response input on the review date.
legal_sources.applies_to: Specified entities and listed cyber incidents; requires a point of contact, reporting within six hours of noticing or being brought to notice, and secure ICT-log retention for 180 days within India.
legal_sources.claim_boundary: The six-hour duty applies to listed cyber incidents within scope; provider-specific subscriber-record duties must not be copied onto every NM customer.

legal_sources.title: Bharatiya Sakshya Adhiniyam, 2023
legal_sources.applies_to: Advocate professional communications, related documents and advice, subject to statutory exceptions; protection continues after professional service ceases and extends to interpreters, clerks and employees.
legal_sources.claim_boundary: Continuing confidentiality is not a universal file-retention period and must not be used to keep every copy indefinitely.

legal_sources.title: Advocates Act, 1961 and Bar Council of India Rules
legal_sources.instrument: Act 25 of 1961, including section 49 rule-making power, and applicable professional-conduct rules
legal_sources.authority: Parliament of India / Bar Council framework / India Code
legal_sources.commencement: The Act and applicable professional rules are current; the exact BCI, State Bar and court rules applicable to the signing advocate and product use must be verified in the signed review.
legal_sources.applies_to: Professional responsibility, conduct, enrolment and the advocate's non-delegable judgment and duties.
legal_sources.claim_boundary: NM may assist; it cannot practise, make the advocate's legal judgment, supply authority to act, or turn a software output into counsel approval.

legal_sources.title: Information Technology (Intermediary Guidelines and Digital Media Ethics Code) Rules, 2021
legal_sources.instrument: Information Technology Rules, 2021 as amended/currently published by MeitY
legal_sources.authority: Ministry of Electronics and Information Technology
legal_sources.commencement: Current rules published under the IT Act; the applicability of intermediary duties depends on NM's actual service and legal classification.
legal_sources.applies_to: Potential intermediary functions, if any; the product name or use of cloud infrastructure does not answer the classification.
legal_sources.claim_boundary: Do not assert safe-harbour status, intermediary duties or non-applicability until qualified counsel reviews the actual information flow and terms.

role_by_purpose.purpose: Account registration, authentication, session control and user support metadata
role_by_purpose.accountability: NM determines the account and security purposes; its approved infrastructure providers act only under recorded instructions.
role_by_purpose.boundary: A firm administrator's separate employment or access-management purposes must be documented rather than implied.

role_by_purpose.purpose: Matter intake, storage, retrieval, analysis, drafting and advice support
role_by_purpose.accountability: The advocate or firm determines the legal-service purpose and remains responsible for instructions, privilege, accuracy and professional judgment; NM enforces the instructed processing boundary.
role_by_purpose.boundary: NM becomes a separate fiduciary for any independent reuse; independent reuse of matter content is prohibited by default.

role_by_purpose.accountability: The firm owns conflict rules and acceptance decisions; NM performs only the recorded check and preserves access separation.
role_by_purpose.boundary: Cross-firm pooling or provider reuse is a new purpose and is prohibited without separate review.

role_by_purpose.purpose: Customer support, diagnosis and service recovery
role_by_purpose.accountability: NM is a fiduciary for support administration and a processor when support accesses matter content under a bounded customer instruction.
role_by_purpose.boundary: Support cannot become standing matter access; approval, purpose, duration and audited withdrawal are required.

role_by_purpose.purpose: Fraud prevention, abuse control, security monitoring and incident compliance
role_by_purpose.accountability: NM determines its service-security purpose and notification operations; the firm separately owns incidents in its practice and its client communications.
role_by_purpose.boundary: Security necessity is not permission for routine matter-content logging or unrelated analytics.

role_by_purpose.purpose: Subscription, invoice, tax and payment administration
role_by_purpose.accountability: NM owns its billing purpose and must separately classify payment providers that determine their own statutory or fraud purposes.
role_by_purpose.boundary: Billing-record duties do not justify retaining the matter corpus.

role_by_purpose.purpose: Advocate-approved export, sharing, filing preparation and receipt capture
role_by_purpose.accountability: The advocate decides recipient, authority and final act; NM prepares and records within the approved mandate.
role_by_purpose.boundary: Recipients may have independent roles; NM does not send or file merely because it prepared a document.

role_by_purpose.purpose: Model training, product improvement, analytics and evaluation
role_by_purpose.accountability: NM would determine this separate purpose and therefore bears the burden of a separate permission and review.
role_by_purpose.boundary: Matter content is excluded by default; provider retention or training is prohibited unless separately reviewed, consented where required and explicitly enabled for an exact population.

permissions.purpose: Create and secure an NM account
permissions.current_position: Collect only data necessary for the service and security purpose with a clear notice and contract; obtain written consent before collecting SPDI where Rule 5 applies.
permissions.future_dpdp_position: Before 13 May 2027 map each item to consent under sections 4 and 6 or a specific section 7 legitimate use; do not assume contract is a standalone DPDP permission.
permissions.reservations: Counsel must confirm the entity, employment/admin flows, SPDI fields and consent design.

permissions.purpose: Process client matter material on the firm's instructions
permissions.current_position: The firm must establish lawful collection and professional authority; NM relies on a scoped services contract and the 2011 processor clarification only to the extent the actual facts fit it, while maintaining Rule 4/security and confidentiality duties.
permissions.future_dpdp_position: The firm must map processing to consent or a specific section 7 use, subject to any necessary section 17 exemption; NM processes only under a valid contract and instruction while the fiduciary remains responsible.
permissions.reservations: Client consent does not automatically cover opponents, witnesses, employees, children or every document in litigation.

permissions.purpose: Process personal data about non-client parties, witnesses and other third persons
permissions.current_position: No blanket consent theory. Record necessity, provenance, professional purpose, disclosure boundary and any court/statutory restriction; apply SPDI and confidentiality controls where relevant.
permissions.future_dpdp_position: Use only a specific consent, legitimate use or exemption that fits the person and purpose; minimise and segregate unsupported material.
permissions.reservations: Counsel must define practice-area rules, vulnerable-person handling and notices or exemptions.

permissions.purpose: Use data where necessary to enforce or defend a legal right or claim
permissions.current_position: Use only to the extent necessary for the legal service, contract and applicable procedural/professional duties; preserve privilege and court restrictions.
permissions.reservations: The exemption must not be applied to every matter, every person or independent product improvement.

permissions.purpose: Protect the service, investigate incidents and meet reporting duties
permissions.current_position: Use present IT Act, CERT-In, contract and security obligations for the necessary minimum; keep routine logs content-free and restrict incident evidence.
permissions.future_dpdp_position: Add operative DPDP safeguards and breach duties from 13 May 2027 without treating them as permission for unrelated monitoring.
permissions.reservations: Sector and contract clocks may impose additional duties.

permissions.purpose: Train models or improve products using matter content
permissions.current_position: No current permission is assumed from service delivery, public filing, account terms or provider defaults.
permissions.future_dpdp_position: Requires a separately reviewed purpose and permission, processor terms, withdrawal/rights operation and exact approved population.
permissions.reservations: De-identification claims require re-identification testing and do not erase privilege or contractual restrictions.

permissions.purpose: Children, biometric/voice identification and other heightened-risk material
permissions.current_position: Do not admit to a live path until the exact purpose, age/authority, consent, recording and sector rules are reviewed.
permissions.future_dpdp_position: Apply the operative child/guardian and prohibited-processing duties when commenced, plus any stricter current law and professional restriction.
permissions.reservations: Voice input for transcription is not automatically voice biometric processing; feature configuration decides and must be proved.

retention.record_class: Matter originals, derivatives, indexes, drafts and advice
retention.current_duty: SPDI Rule 5(4), where applicable, requires no longer than purpose or other law; privilege/confidentiality continues after service but does not impose indefinite storage.
retention.ordinary_rule: A counsel-approved schedule per matter class, posture and client terms; derivative lineage follows the source.
retention.hold_rule: A scoped legal hold suspends only conflicting destruction, names authority, custodian, population, start, review and release.
retention.erasure_restore_rule: Write tombstones across originals, derivatives and indexes; a restored backup must replay later tombstones before exposure.

retention.record_class: Identity, authentication, sessions, notices and account preferences
retention.current_duty: Retain only for current account/security purposes and separately identified statutory claims or records.
retention.ordinary_rule: Delete or irreversibly separate obsolete account data after closure and security windows, preserving only justified audit facts.
retention.hold_rule: A claim, investigation or lawful order may hold the exact account records it identifies.
retention.erasure_restore_rule: Revoked sessions remain revoked after restore; deleted identity data cannot silently reappear.

retention.current_duty: CERT-In directions require secure retention of ICT logs for 180 days within Indian jurisdiction for covered entities; collect content-free events wherever possible.
retention.ordinary_rule: Keep the applicable maximum of current floors and the approved security purpose, then delete on schedule.
retention.hold_rule: An incident or lawful investigation may hold a bounded subset with chain of custody.
retention.erasure_restore_rule: Log deletion and hold release apply to archives and restored copies; never retain routine privileged content to satisfy a log-duration rule.

retention.record_class: Incident evidence, notices, decisions and custody records
retention.current_duty: Preserve what is necessary for containment, reporting, investigation and claims; no universal duration is asserted.
retention.ordinary_rule: Use a separate restricted incident schedule and minimise duplicated matter content.
retention.hold_rule: Active investigation, regulator request, court order or claim controls the identified evidence until formal release.
retention.erasure_restore_rule: Close with a custody and deletion decision; restored evidence stays restricted and respects later disposition.

retention.current_duty: Backups are not an indefinite exception to purpose limitation, contract, holds or deletion.
retention.ordinary_rule: Document rotation, deletion latency, region, keys and achieved recovery points; expire generations on schedule.
retention.hold_rule: Hold only the necessary recoverable population and document why ordinary rotation cannot satisfy it.
retention.erasure_restore_rule: Restore into quarantine, replay access revocations and tombstones, then expose only authorised current state.

retention.record_class: Counsel qualification, authority and signed approval evidence
retention.current_duty: Retain a restricted authority artifact or trusted reference and original-byte digest sufficient to verify who could decide the exact scope.
retention.ordinary_rule: Repository stores only the minimum identity, authority basis, restricted reference, digest, dates and decision scope.
retention.hold_rule: Preserve challenged, superseded and revoked decision history; do not overwrite it with the replacement.
retention.erasure_restore_rule: Redact or delete excess personal data without destroying the auditable decision identity required for accountability.

incident_clocks.trigger: Any credible security or confidentiality event
incident_clocks.recipient: Incident commander, privacy/legal owner and backup contact
incident_clocks.minimum_action: Open the incident, preserve time and custody, contain safely, start every potentially applicable clock and record unknowns.
incident_clocks.boundary: Internal target is not represented as a statutory deadline and does not delay an earlier external duty.

incident_clocks.trigger: A listed cyber incident is noticed or brought to notice within the scope of the CERT-In directions
incident_clocks.minimum_action: Report available information within six hours and supplement; do not wait for a complete root-cause analysis.
incident_clocks.boundary: Counsel and the incident commander classify coverage promptly; the direction is not a six-hour clock for every support issue.

incident_clocks.trigger: Knowledge of a personal data breach after the relevant DPDP duties commence
incident_clocks.owner: The applicable Data Fiduciary with OWNER-PRIVACY-LEGAL
incident_clocks.minimum_action: Provide the rule 7 content in concise and clear form through the registered account or communication method.
incident_clocks.boundary: Future design requirement on the review date; it must not be described as the present DPDP notification clock.

incident_clocks.trigger: Knowledge of a personal data breach after the relevant DPDP duties commence
incident_clocks.owner: The applicable Data Fiduciary with OWNER-PRIVACY-LEGAL
incident_clocks.minimum_action: Send the initial known description without delay and the detailed rule 7 report within 72 hours unless the Board permits a longer period.
incident_clocks.boundary: The future 72-hour detailed report does not replace the immediate first notice or the current CERT-In six-hour assessment.

incident_clocks.trigger: A processor, client, insurer or other contract defines a security/confidentiality notification event
incident_clocks.minimum_action: Run the contractual notice in parallel and preserve proof of timing and content.
incident_clocks.boundary: A contract can be shorter or broader than statute but cannot waive a mandatory public-law duty.

incident_clocks.trigger: The matter, entity, order or regulated sector creates another reporting or preservation duty
incident_clocks.recipient: Court, regulator, law-enforcement body, client or other named recipient
incident_clocks.minimum_action: Identify the instrument, trigger, time unit, recipient, authorised content and conflict with privilege before release.
incident_clocks.boundary: No universal sector or court clock is asserted for NM's India-only service.

accountability.role: Firm accountable partner or sole advocate
accountability.answerable_for: Matter purpose, client authority, conflicts, third-party data, privilege, legal holds, advice and external action.
accountability.cannot_delegate: Professional judgment, client duty and final legal approval cannot be transferred to NM or a model.

accountability.answerable_for: Account, billing and independent service purposes; notices, minimisation, product defaults and purpose changes.
accountability.cannot_delegate: NM's own fiduciary purposes cannot be relabelled customer processing by contract prose.

accountability.answerable_for: Instrument register, permission mapping, rights, retention conflicts, breach classification and legal-change review.
accountability.cannot_delegate: A framework, vendor certificate or agent-generated answer cannot make the legal applicability decision.
accountability.required_before: BK-85-AC3 is signed and each live-data gate is considered.

accountability.role: Named CERT-In point of contact and backup
accountability.answerable_for: Current contact registration, six-hour assessment/reporting route, time source and secure log availability.
accountability.cannot_delegate: Provider notification does not prove NM's own applicable notice was made.

accountability.answerable_for: Detection time, containment, clock ledger, evidence custody, communications, recovery and post-incident review.
accountability.cannot_delegate: Incomplete facts are recorded and supplemented; they cannot be treated as a reason to let a clock expire.
accountability.required_before: Any real data or externally reachable deployment.

accountability.answerable_for: Schedules, holds, releases, lineage, erasure, tombstones, backup replay and deletion evidence.
accountability.cannot_delegate: A storage lifecycle setting does not decide legal holds or prove physical deletion across derivatives.

accountability.answerable_for: Inventory, contract, region, purpose, training/retention settings, subprocessor change, exit and incident route.
accountability.cannot_delegate: Vendor availability or a procurement approval cannot grant processing permission.
accountability.required_before: Any provider can receive protected data.

accountability.answerable_for: Dated applicability judgment, professional-rule position, material reservations and expiry/reassessment triggers.
accountability.cannot_delegate: Only a stated and evidenced qualified reviewer can sign counsel_review evidence.
accountability.required_before: BK-85-AC3 can confer PASS or inform live-data approvals.

accountability.answerable_for: Exact release manifest, current evidence, reservations, approvals, rollback and the enabled scope.
accountability.cannot_delegate: A green plan, stale review or approval for another gate cannot release this scope.

review_reservations.question: What are the exact NM and customer legal entities, contracting relationships and actual instructions for every purpose?
review_reservations.review_evidence: Executed service terms, entity chart and purpose/data-flow inventory.

review_reservations.question: Which Bar Council, State Bar, Telangana/other High Court and professional-conduct rules govern the first users and tasks?
review_reservations.review_evidence: Official current rules and a task-specific professional-duty memorandum.

review_reservations.question: Does any NM function make it an intermediary, and what safe-harbour or due-diligence duties follow?
review_reservations.review_evidence: Actual information flow, terms, content control and qualified IT Act/Rules classification.

review_reservations.question: Which sector, matter and vulnerable-person rules apply to health, finance, employment, sexual-offence, child, biometric, recording or sealed material?
review_reservations.review_evidence: Separate enabled-data manifest and official sector/procedural instruments.

review_reservations.question: What purpose-specific retention terms, client instructions, tax/company records and litigation-hold rules apply?
review_reservations.review_evidence: Approved schedule, hold protocol, contract matrix and tested deletion/restore lineage.

review_reservations.question: Which processors, subprocessors, models, regions, retention/training options and support paths will the exact release use?
review_reservations.review_evidence: Signed processor terms and immutable release/configuration/data-flow manifests.

review_reservations.question: What lawful permission or exemption covers each present and future purpose and each third-person population?
review_reservations.review_evidence: Purpose-by-purpose signed legal mapping and product enforcement proof.

review_reservations.question: Which client, insurer, provider, court and sector incident clocks supplement CERT-In and future DPDP duties?
review_reservations.review_evidence: Contract/instrument clock register, named contacts and timed no-send rehearsal.

review_reservations.question: Has the 16 December 2025 DPDP Rules corrigendum and every later Gazette notification changed a proposition in this packet?
review_reservations.review_evidence: Dated Gazette search log and reviewed consolidated instrument set.

review_reservations.question: Who is authorised to sign for product, firm, privacy/legal, security, operations and counsel at the exact gate?
review_reservations.review_evidence: Delegation records and restricted authority artifacts with original-byte SHA-256 digests.

reassessment_triggers: Before 13 November 2026 and before 13 May 2027, even if no other change occurs.
Any new Gazette notification, corrigendum, rule, binding judgment, CERT-In direction or regulator/court requirement affecting a recorded proposition.
Any new legal entity, jurisdiction, State Bar/court, practice area, professional role, language, data class or coverage pack.
Any new or changed processor, subprocessor, model, region, cross-border route, retention/training setting, support path or security telemetry sink.
Any change to purpose, permission, notice, terms, client authority, retention schedule, hold operation or external action capability.
Any material incident, failed control, regulator/client challenge, professional complaint or evidence that a role classification is wrong.
Any confidential-pilot or production approval expiry, revocation, supersession or relevant release/configuration change.
At the qualified reviewer's earlier chosen valid_until date.

counsel_signoff.required_reviewer: An Indian-qualified advocate or equivalent authorised Indian legal reviewer must verify the official instruments, the actual product/entities/contracts and every reservation. The reviewer must state the authority basis and reference a restricted evidence artifact with its original-byte SHA-256 digest.

authority_shape.basis: State Bar enrolment or equivalent legal authority, including jurisdiction and current standing basis

evidence.ref: Restricted authority artifact reference; do not commit unnecessary personal data
evidence.sha256: 64 lower-case hexadecimal characters over the original artifact bytes

counsel_signoff.validity_rule: The reviewer chooses valid_until. It must be finite and should be no later than the earliest material trigger or 13 November 2026; renewal requires a new dated review rather than editing history.
counsel_signoff.signing_instruction: Resolve or expressly carry every material reservation; set result to PASS only if the rubric is satisfied for the counted population; record remaining reservations as an array; place the completed record at the target path and update BK-85-AC3 to reference it. A template is generated beside this packet but is deliberately invalid until completed and signed.

approval_packets.approver: product owner and qualified Indian counsel
required_inputs: exact India jurisdiction/entity and Telangana/Union coverage manifest
approver authority evidence and signed expiring record
conditions: A new jurisdiction, task, language, court or practice pack requires a new exact-scope record.
India-only is product scope; do not claim blanket statutory localisation.
approval_packets.must_not_claim: No confidential data or coverage pack is authorised by this prepared packet.

approval_packets.approver: qualified Indian counsel and data owner
required_inputs: approver authority evidence and signed expiring record
conditions: Public availability is not redistribution permission.
Synthetic evaluation labels cannot become legal gold labels.
approval_packets.must_not_claim: The existence of a source file or passing retrieval test does not approve legal use or publication.

required_inputs: current signed BK-85-AC3 review and incident clock register
measured restore and incident rehearsal evidence
approver authority evidence and signed expiring record
conditions: Proposed RPO <=15 minutes and RTO <=4 hours are not promises until achieved, priced and approved.
Ordinary acknowledged writes cannot be lost during process restart.
All current and future applicable clocks remain distinct.
approval_packets.must_not_claim: A synthetic restore or tabletop is not production recovery or notification proof.

approval_packets.approver: product owner, engineering, security/privacy and qualified counsel reviewers
required_inputs: exact immutable release, configuration, coverage and processor/model manifests
current criterion evidence and gate report
all joint approver authority evidence and signed expiring record
conditions: Approval cannot convert FAIL, NOT_RUN or STALE evidence into PASS.
Any relevant manifest/configuration, processor, capability, data class or coverage change makes the record stale or out of scope.
approval_packets.must_not_claim: A green plan, packet build or unrelated approval cannot admit confidential pilot or production.
